transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-21
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Leah Moreno (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood Solutions Eng), Nina Cho (CTO - Elysium Care), Rajiv Menon (Platform Eng), Jill Harper (Head of MLOps), Evan Lo (SRE)

Topics: benchmark delta (latency/throughput), dedicated slots, routing fallback, security gating (SOC2/VPC/KMS), next steps

00:00 Samir: okay everyone thanks for joining today's weekly POC velocity deep dive, we've got about an hour. Quick roll call?
00:08 Nina: Nina here.
00:10 Rajiv: Rajiv.
00:12 Jill: Jill — hi.
00:14 Leah: Leah from Redwood, hi all.
00:16 Samir: and Diego will jump on at the end for the infra bit. We circulated the week-2 summary and the new bench csvs — any immediate blockers?
00:30 Rajiv: nothing blocking, just excited to see the tail numbers. Our baseline provider — IncumbentAI — has been consistent but cost is high.
01:02 Samir: great. Quick agenda: we walk the benchmark spreadsheet Samir/Leah annotated, call out where numbers came from, dig into p50/p95/p99 for 512/2k/8k token profiles, discuss routing and cache behavior, then security and next steps.
02:15 Leah: starting slide deck, the first table shows p50/p95 for short convo profile (512 tokens): Redwood Dedicated slot with prefix caching, p50 38ms, p95 112ms, p99 198ms. IncumbentAI p50 42ms, p95 140ms, p99 260ms — so smaller tail on Redwood for short queries. Note: these are median across 10k requests sampled from your traffic.
04:05 Jill: can I ask about sampling? our traffic has a bimodal token distribution; the sample should weight the long medical notes higher — otherwise p99 is understated.
04:28 Leah: good call — we used the sampling you provided last week which was uniform across sessions; we also ran weighted runs, those are in tab 3 of the csv. The weighted run moves p95/p99 up, but again Redwood's delta vs incumbent shrinks but remains favorable on short profiles.
06:10 Rajiv: what about throughput? Incumbent has been able to handle sustained 600 rps at 512 tokens with 95th under 200ms. Can Redwood match that peak throughput in dedicated mode?
06:42 Samir: our dedicated slot with 8x V100-equivalent GPUs sustained 580 rps with p95 210ms in our cloud nodes during the run. There was some variance because of cold KV cache early in the run. After warmup, p95 moved to 180ms.
07:30 Evan: are those numbers single-model or with routing to cheaper quantized variants? because we noticed incumbent switches to a quantized instance during peaks.
07:50 Leah: we kept the model constant to be apples-to-apples, no automatic fallback during the run. We did a second pass with quantized 4-bit model and saw unit-cost drop ~40% but p95 increased about 30ms on 512 tokens; details in the quant table.
09:12 Nina: the 8k token tail is our real concern — medical summaries often hit long contexts. What's Redwood's p95 for 8k?
09:30 Leah: for 8k sequence: Redwood p50 220ms, p95 1.1s, p99 2.4s (note these are with KV cache enabled, which helps when the prefix is repetitive). Incumbent had p95 950ms and p99 2.1s in our runs — so incumbent slightly better on sustained 8k tails in our lab. But we think dedicated-slot tuning and kernel selection can close that gap.
11:05 Rajiv: hmm interesting. Did your test use the same beam/sample settings as production? our prod uses top-p 0.9 and temperature 0.2 and uses streaming so perceived latency is lower for users.
11:28 Leah: we ran both streaming and non-streaming measures; the numbers I quoted are generation-complete latency (non-streaming). Streaming first-byte latencies are ~30-50% lower and are in the stream tab.
12:20 Jill: can you explain KV cache behavior? sometimes our prompts re-use large clinical prefix templates so cache hit ratio matters a lot.
12:45 Leah: yes — our prefix/KV caching works across requests when the prefix matches; in your traffic the hit-rate was ~42% for the last week sample. That reduced per-token compute substantially. The exporter had an intermittent bug that logged hit-rate as 0 for a subset of runs — that's why you'll see a few outliers in the raw logs.
13:58 Rajiv: that might explain the cold-starts we saw at the 10 minute mark.
14:10 Samir: we re-ran the warmup sequence this morning and attached both the raw logs and the annotated diffs. The diffs highlight where the K V cash — sorry — KV cache warmed and made the biggest difference.
15:05 Nina: ha, K V cash, yeah. Are there network differences that could bias the comparison? our baseline runs in eu-west while Redwood ran in us-west in your shared runs.
15:28 Samir: good catch — the runs we showed were us-west. We also ran eu-west tests; eu-west p95 was ~20ms higher overall due to region egress; I'll mark that in the spreadsheet.
16:40 Evan: on security, how do you handle key management? we're required to manage keys via our HSM and rotate keys quarterly.
17:05 Samir: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM; for hosted we have envelope encryption with KMS integration. We'll share SOC2 + VPC architecture notes.
18:32 Jill: and audit logs? we need per-request logs for compliance and must be able to tie back to an SSO identity for sequence runs.
18:50 Leah: we capture request-level metadata and trace IDs; for Private we can stream detailed audit logs into your S3 bucket or SIEM. There are retention policy options.
20:12 Nina: coming back to perf, you mentioned dedicated-slot tuning — what's that operationally?
20:30 Leah: dedicated slots are reserved GPU pools for you. We can assign different kernel/compilation flags, pre-warm KV caches per slot, and pin model versions. Operationally it reduces jitter from noisy neighbors and gives predictable tail latency. The tradeoff is reserved capacity cost.
22:00 Rajiv: cost is material — incumbent's committed price includes a discount. What cost delta should we expect with dedicated?
22:20 Samir: rough math from our runs: for your current 600 rps sustained 512-token profile, Redwood hosted auto with batching is ~15% lower unit cost; dedicated reserved slots are about on-par or slightly higher than incumbent unless you commit a longer term. But with quantization and caching you can reduce unit cost further. We'll provide an exact breakdown in the sheet.
24:05 Nina: can we do a head-to-head where both providers run in eu-west with identical traffic for the 8k profile? that's the most useful for the team.
24:25 Samir: yes, we can replicate in eu-west. Leah — can you schedule a dedicated-slot run in eu-west and coordinate with Rajiv on traffic replay?
24:40 Leah: yes, I'll coordinate. I'll need Rajiv's traffic replay and token distribution artifact.
25:05 Rajiv: I'll upload the traffic file to the shared folder by EOD. There was also a note about warmup duration; our production sees diurnal bursts — we want to test sustained 30 minute windows.
26:00 Leah: we'll run a 30 minute sustained test with 5 minute warmup and capture p50/p95/p99 and breakdown by seq len.
27:12 Jill: on the fallback strategies — if Redwood hits capacity we need graceful degradation back to incumbent. Do you support automatic fallback routing?
27:25 Samir: yes, we have smart routing policies; you can route by latency, cost, region, or model compatibility. For pilot we usually prefer manual failover until we tune thresholds.
28:05 Evan: any limitations with streaming + fallback? we want to avoid re-stream duplication for users.
28:20 Leah: we have re-stream idempotency tokens to avoid double responses during fallback. It's in the SDK notes.
29:50 Nina: what about AVX/FP kernel differences? incumbent mentioned custom kernel libs.
30:10 Leah: Redwood's runtime selects kernels at load-time and can use optimized attention kernels and fused ops; however certain proprietary kernel libraries from incumbents can outperform in narrow cases. That's why we do head-to-head on the same hardware.
31:40 Rajiv: curious about the p99 outliers — some of the Redwood p99 spikes coincided with GC or node restarts?
32:05 Leah: the p99 spikes earlier were due to a stray housekeeping job that ran on the host during two windows; we identified and blacklisted that job in the test config. The raw logs show the timestamps.
33:20 Samir: Diego joined now for the infra deep dive — Diego, quick summary?
33:35 Diego: hi all — from infra, we recommend dedicated slots with pre-warm scripts for your heavy 8k flows. We'll also enable a KV cache eviction policy tuned to your prefix length. For on-prem plan we need your NIC specs and RDMA availability.
34:50 Evan: RDMA is not available in our colo; it's standard TCP only. Any impact?
35:05 Diego: we can adjust kernel selection for TCP-only; there will be some throughput impact but it's manageable. We'll quantify in the upcoming run.
36:30 Jill: will you be able to provide an estimate of nodes / GPU count needed for our 600 rps 512 mixed with 50 rps 8k sustained?
36:50 Diego: preliminary estimate: 6 dedicated GPUs for the 512-heavy baseline plus 2 additional for the 8k sustained workload to avoid interference; we'll produce a sizing doc.
38:10 Rajiv: ok good. Are there any experimental features that could help reduce 8k p95? we heard about windowed attention and chunked KV strategies.
38:32 Leah: we have a chunked attention mode that trades slight quality for compute; in some tests it reduced p95 by ~200ms on 8k. We can run a QA pass on your prompt sets to check quality delta.
40:00 Nina: quality is non-negotiable; if chunking alters clinical accuracy we can't take it. We'll need evals on our clinical prompts.
40:20 Leah: understood — we'll run a quality regression on the exact prompt set and flag any differences.
41:45 Samir: quick note on observability — Redwood Console will give you token-level cost and per-request trace IDs; we'll open a read-only account for Elysium so your SREs can see live dashboards.
42:10 Evan: provide read-only for SREs please. We need to check trace correlation with our logs.
42:25 Samir: will do.
43:00 Jill: timeline question — if we like the eu-west head-to-head, how long to move to a short pilot with dedicated slots in production?
43:20 Samir: typically 2-4 weeks after sign-off: one week for provisioning and infra smoke tests, one week for warmup and tuning, then pilot window. If you want on-prem, add 2-3 more weeks.
44:05 Rajiv: procurement will ask about SLA — what's your typical p95 SLA for dedicated?
44:18 Samir: we offer latency SLAs for Dedicated customers in contract — baseline p95 targets are customizable; the commercial team will send SLA language.
45:00 Nina: ok let's recap actions.
45:05 Samir: recap: 1) Samir share annotated benchmark csv & raw logs by tomorrow, 2) Leah run eu-west dedicated-slot 8k tail test and post logs, 3) Rajiv to upload traffic replay, 4) Redwood to share SOC2 + VPC + KMS docs, 5) schedule infra prerequisites call Dec 2. Any additions?
45:45 Jill: can you also include the quantization table and note which quant profiles were used?
45:55 Leah: yes will include quant table and exact flags.
46:15 Evan: also include network test artifacts (iperf/latency) for the eu-west runs.
46:25 Samir: good point — we'll add that.
47:50 Nina: thanks team — overall we're cautiously optimistic; the short-token delta favors Redwood which is promising for chat UX, but we need the 8k head-to-head before committing.
48:05 Samir: understood. We'll prioritize the eu-west 8k run.
48:30 Diego: infra note — I'll attach the sizing doc draft and an RDMA/no-RDMA comparison.
49:10 Rajiv: I'll aim to upload traffic file by EOD.
49:30 Samir: any other quick Qs?
50:02 Jill: one small ask — can you include an end-to-end example of a traced request including SSO identity, trace id, and cost breakdown?
50:20 Leah: yes, we'll attach a sample traced request anonymized.
51:00 Samir: perfect. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and schedule the Dec 2 infra call.
51:15 Nina: thanks.
51:20 Rajiv: thanks all.
51:25 Diego: thanks, bye.
51:30 Meeting ends.
